chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to him (peace be upon him), 'A man married a woman, so he touched her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is prohibited to his father and his son, and her dower is obligatory.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife's prohibition to her husband's father and son after consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling of 'marriage with consummation' (nikah with dhawr) establishing that the wife becomes permanently prohibited to the husband's father and son, a ruling derived from the principle of 'haram li-ghayrihi' (prohibited to others due to her status). The mention of the obligatory dowry underscores that consummation validates the financial rights of the wife even if the marriage contract is later found to be defective or voidable. This reflects the Shia juristic consensus that physical intimacy solidifies the marital bond's prohibitions and financial obligations.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Hassan Bin iyad, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man married a woman, so he touches her’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is Pohibited unto his father, and his son, and her dower is Obligated’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from al-Hassan ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has married a woman and has touched her. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘She is unlawful to his father and her mahr (dower) is obligatory.’”
